text: If you are distressed by anything external, the pain is not due to the thing itself, but to your estimate of it; and this you have the power to revoke at any moment.
author: Marcus Aurelius

text: I never think of the future. It comes soon enough.
author: Albert Einstein

text: Pay attention to your enemies, for they are the first to discover your mistakes.
author: Antisthenes

text: Let us endeavor so to live that when we come to die even the undertaker will be sorry.
author: Mark Twain

text: The unexamined life is not worth living.
author: Socrates

text: Society is always taken by surprise at any new example of common sense.
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

text: Anyone who has no need of anybody but himself is either a beast or a God.
author: Aristotle

text: A ship is safe in harbor, but that's not what ships are for.
author: John A. Shedd

text: Whoever knows the All but fails to know himself lacks everything.
author: Gospel of Thomas

text: The mind is its own place, and in itself can make a heaven of hell, a hell of heaven.
author: John Milton

text: What does not benefit the hive is no benefit to the bee.
author: Marcus Aurelius

text: For the strength of the Pack is the Wolf, and the strength of the Wolf is the Pack.
author: Rudyard Kipling
source: The Law of the Jungle, The Second Jungle Book (1895)

text: He who has a Why to live for can bear almost any How.
author: Friedrich Nietzsche

text: The most useful piece of learning for the uses of life is to unlearn what is untrue.
author: Antisthenes

text: There are more things, Lucilius, that frighten us than inspire us, and we suffer more in imagination than in reality.
author: Seneca

text: The secret of success is constancy to purpose.
author: Benjamin Disraeli

text: The crowning fortune of a man is to be born to some pursuit which finds him employment and happiness, whether it be to make baskets, or broadswords, or canals, or statues, or songs.
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

text: It isn't what you have or who you are or where you are or what you are doing that makes you happy or unhappy. It is what you think about it.
author: Dale Carnegie
source: How to Win Friends and Influence People (1936)

text: The important thing is not to stop questioning. Curiosity has its own reason for existing.
author: Albert Einstein

text: The most beautiful thing we can experience is the mysterious. It is the source of all true art and all science. He to whom this emotion is a stranger, who can no longer pause to wonder and stand rapt in awe, is as good as dead: his eyes are closed.
author: Albert Einstein
source: The World as I See It (1931)

text: Action may not always bring happiness; but there is no happiness without action.
author: Benjamin Disraeli

text: Knowledge is the antidote to fear.
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

text: Very little is needed to make a happy life; it is all within yourself in your way of thinking.
author: Marcus Aurelius

text: Do not spoil what you have by desiring what you have not; remember that what you now have was once among the things you only hoped for.
author: Epicurus

text: I am the master of my fate, I am the captain of my soul.
author: William Ernest Henley

text: After the final no there comes a yes.
author: Wallace Stevens
source: The Well Dressed Man with a Beard (1941)

text: Creation is a better means of self-expression than possession; it is through creating, not possessing, that life is revealed.
author: Vida D. Scudder
source: The Life of the Spirit in the Modern English Poets (1895)

text: How much pain have cost us the evils which have never happened.
author: Thomas Jefferson

text: Imagination is more important than knowledge.
author: Albert Einstein

text: Great spirits have often encountered violent opposition from weak minds.
author: Albert Einstein

text: A human being is a part of a whole, called by us universe, a part limited in time and space. He experiences himself, his thoughts and feelings as something separated from the rest... a kind of optical delusion of his consciousness. This delusion is a kind of prison for us, restricting us to our personal desires and to affection for a few persons nearest to us. Our task must be to free ourselves from this prison by widening our circle of compassion to embrace all living creatures and the whole of nature in its beauty.
author: Albert Einstein
